item.title: Tuba Hassan’s three-wicket haul guides Pakistan to victory over Bangladesh in Emerging Nations Trophy
item.description:
Tuba Hassan’s three-wicket haul and an unbeaten partnership between captain Muneeba Ali and Ayesha Zafar helped Pakistan beat Bangladesh by eight wickets in their Group ‘B’ match of the ICC Women’s Emerging Nations Trophy at the Karwan Sports Club Cricket Ground in Ajman on Thursday.

After opting to bowl, Pakistan restricted Bangladesh to 108-9 in their allotted 20 overs through a disciplined bowling performance led by Tuba, who claimed three wickets for 26 runs. Left-arm spinner Nashra Sundhu also impressed, taking two wickets for 13 runs.

Bangladesh appeared to be in a reasonable position at 52-2 before their innings suffered a dramatic collapse. They lost five wickets for just 16 runs as Pakistan tightened their grip on the match.

Tuba triggered the slide by dismissing Sharmin Akter for nine before removing Bangladesh captain Nigar Sultana Joty, who scored 27, and Ritu Moni for two.

Nashra provided further breakthroughs to keep the opposition under pressure, while Shorna Akter offered some resistance with an unbeaten 21 to help Bangladesh cross the 100-run mark. Nigar’s 27 remained the highest individual score for her side.

In reply, Pakistan made a brisk start, with Shawaal Zulfiqar striking four boundaries in a six-ball 16 before departing early.

Sadaf Shamas then steadied the innings with a valuable 37, helping Pakistan reach 68-2 at the halfway stage and keeping the required run rate comfortably within reach.

Captain Muneeba and Ayesha completed the chase without further loss, putting together an unbeaten 44-run stand for the third wicket.

Muneeba remained not out on 31, while Ayesha contributed an unbeaten 27 as Pakistan reached 112-2 in 15.5 overs, sealing victory with 25 balls to spare.

Bangladesh’s Sobhana Mostary and Shorna took one wicket apiece, but their efforts were insufficient to prevent Pakistan from securing a comprehensive win.

The victory was built on Pakistan’s effective bowling after Bangladesh had made a steady start, with Tuba’s strikes in the middle overs proving decisive.

Pakistan’s batters then ensured there was no late drama, completing the chase comfortably to strengthen their position in Group ‘B’.

item.title: Pakistan set up India final after Rizwanullah’s five-for sinks Bangladesh in U-19 Asia Cup
item.description:
Pakistan will face arch-rivals India in the final of the Under-19 Asia Cup after both sides won their respective semi-finals on Thursday, with fast bowler Rizwanullah leading the defending champions to a nine-wicket victory over Bangladesh.

India booked their place in Saturday’s title clash after defeating Afghanistan in the second semi-final, setting up a highly anticipated encounter between the subcontinent rivals.

During the match against Bangladesh, Pakistan bundled out the opposition for 138 in 31.4 overs after opting to bowl, with Rizwanullah leading the attack with figures of five for 30 from eight overs.

Left-arm pacer Mohammad Sayyam chipped in with two wickets for 29 runs as Pakistan’s bowlers kept the opposition under sustained pressure.

Bangladesh struggled to build partnerships, losing three of their top five batters for single-digit scores. Opener Abdullah Al Muhi provided some resistance with a 50 off 45 deliveries, striking four fours and two sixes, but his dismissal in the 14th over triggered a collapse from which Bangladesh failed to recover.

Pakistan then made light work of the modest target, reaching 141 for one in 21.5 overs.

Openers Hayam Khan and Usman Khan laid the foundation for the emphatic chase with a 123-run partnership. Hayam struck a fluent 69 off 72 balls, hitting eight fours and a six, before falling to Robiul Hasan.

Usman remained unbeaten on 64 from 54 deliveries, his innings featuring seven fours and two sixes. He finished the contest in emphatic fashion, striking a boundary and a six off consecutive deliveries.

The victory extended Pakistan’s unbeaten run in the tournament, having previously defeated the United Arab Emirates, India and Nepal in the group stage.

90-day credit facility on 11 commodities imports to curb price hikes ahead of Ramadan
item.description:
Ahead of Ramadan, Bangladesh Bank has allowed the import of 11 essential food commodities under deferred payment facilities to keep market prices affordable and ensure steady supplies.

The central bank issued a circular to this effect today, Wednesday.

According to the directive, importers will be entitled to a deferred payment facility of up to 90 days for importing rice, wheat, onions, pulses, soybean oil, palm oil, sugar, chickpeas, spices, dates and peas.

Bangladesh Bank said this special facility was extended to keep supplies smooth and prices manageable during the Ramadan.

Importers will be able to avail of this credit facility for up to 90 days under suppliers' credit or buyers' credit.

Under this facility, importers will not be required to settle the full import bill immediately upon the arrival of the consignment in the country. Instead, they will have the opportunity to pay the import value at the end of the stipulated period on a deferred basis.

This will allow importers to clear their bank liabilities after selling the goods in the domestic market. Central bank officials believe the move will ease working capital pressures on importers.

Demand for commodities such as rice, pulses, onions, edible oil, sugar, chickpeas and dates typically surges in the country during Ramadan.

Ensuring uninterrupted supplies and reducing price pressure in the retail market become crucial during this period. Banking sector insiders believe this fresh central bank decision will encourage traders to import these essential goods.

Bangladesh Bank stated that this new facility will remain in effect until March 15 next year.

Earlier on 8 November, Bangladesh Bank instructed commercial banks to keep cash margins at a minimum level based on banker-customer relationships when opening letters of credit (LCs) for importing these commodities ahead of Ramadan.

The items were rice, wheat, onions, pulses, soybean oil, palm oil, sugar, chickpeas, peas, spices, and dates.

An LC margin is the specific percentage of cash or security an importer must deposit with a bank when opening an import letter of credit. For example, if a 100 percent margin is imposed, the entire value of the imported goods must be deposited in cash to open an LC.

When the margin requirement is kept at a minimum or relaxed, opening an LC becomes feasible with significantly lower upfront cash deposits based on mutual trust and relations with the bank.

item.title: Why ACC’s press briefing on Asif Mahmud is not illegal: HC
item.description:
The High Court has issued a rule questioning the legality of the Anti-Corruption Commission's (ACC) press briefings concerning Asif Mahmud Shojib Bhuyain, former adviser to the interim government and leader of the National Citizen Party (NCP).

The rule was issued on Wednesday by a High Court bench comprising Justice Md Bashir Ullah and Justice Md Hamidur Rahman after an initial hearing on a writ petition filed by Asif Mahmud.

He filed the petition in September, challenging the legality of an ACC press briefing in which the commission announced that it had found “preliminary evidence” after deciding to investigate allegations of corruption and money laundering against him.

The rule asks why the ACC press briefings, held on 2 and 13 September by its deputy director and assistant director, announcing that “preliminary evidence” had been found following the decision to investigate the allegations, should not be declared illegal and beyond lawful authority for violating Article 31 of the Constitution and the ACC's Information Disclosure Policy, 2011.

The court also asked why the ACC should not be directed to refrain from holding press briefings on any ongoing inquiry or investigation.

The hearing on Asif Mahmud's writ petition took place on 4 November. After hearing the petition, the court set this Wednesday for its order.

Senior lawyer Mohammod Hossain, along with lawyers Yousuf Ali and Zahirul Islam Musa, represented the petitioner. Lawyer Mohammad Mahbubur Rahman Khan appeared for the ACC.

Confirming the issuance of the rule, lawyer Zahirul Islam Musa told Prothom Alo that the ACC chairman, deputy director, public relations officer and assistant director had been asked to respond to the rule within four weeks.

According to the petitioner's lawyers, the ACC's deputy director and public relations officer, along with an assistant director, held two press briefings on 2 and 13 September.

At the briefings, the commission said it had found “preliminary evidence” after deciding to investigate allegations of corruption and money laundering against Asif Mahmud.

The briefings violated the protection of dignity and reputation guaranteed under Article 31 of the Constitution and the ACC's Right to Information Disclosure Guidelines, the lawyers argued.

The Awami League government fell on 5 August 2024 following the July Mass Uprising. An interim government led by Professor Muhammad Yunus was formed on 8 August that year.

As a representative of the students who led the July uprising, Asif Mahmud joined the interim government as an adviser. He was initially in charge of the Ministry of Labour and Employment and the Ministry of Youth and Sports.

In November 2024, he was given charge of the Ministry of Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives. He subsequently served as adviser to both the local government and youth and sports ministries.

Asif Mahmud resigned from the interim government in December 2025. Later that month, he formally joined the National Citizen Party (NCP). He is currently the party's senior joint member secretary.

item.title: Biman flights on Dhaka–Riyadh–Dhaka route suspended for 19 days
item.description:
Considering the attack-related situation in Saudi Arabia and the safety of passengers, Biman Bangladesh Airlines has decided to extend the suspension of flights on the Riyadh route for another 19 days.

Regular flights on the Dhaka-Riyadh-Dhaka route will be suspended until 30 November.

This information was provided by Biman Bangladesh Airlines in a press release this Wednesday afternoon.

The statement mentioned that in light of the recent airstrike-related situation in Saudi Arabia and concerns over passenger safety, the previously made decisions regarding the operation of flights to Saudi Arabia will remain in effect until 30 November.

However, flights on the Dhaka-Jeddah, Dhaka-Dammam, and Dhaka-Madinah routes will continue as per the earlier announcements and schedules.

Passengers are requested to contact the nearest Biman sales centre for updated information on tickets and travel.

Earlier, on 25 October, the suspension period of flights on the Dhaka-Dammam and Dhaka-Riyadh routes was extended until 4 November.

Later, the company announced the resumption of regular flights on the Dhaka-Dammam-Dhaka route starting 7 November.

However, it was decided to keep the Riyadh route's flights suspended until further notice.

The Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB) reported on 8 November that 186 flights operating directly or via transit between Bangladesh and Saudi Arabia were disrupted due to restrictions on flight operations following attacks by Iran-supported Yemeni armed group Houthis at various Saudi Arabian airports. Among these, there were 109 direct flights.

item.title: COP31 pledge targets $156b annual investment to boost electrification
item.description:
Governments, energy agencies and businesses have pledged to accelerate global electrification, with an annual investment commitment of $156 billion for power grids, renewable energy and storage announced at the COP31 climate summit on Tuesday.
The COP31 35-by-35 Global Electrification Pledge aims to raise electricity’s share of global final energy consumption from around 23% to at least 35% by 2035, accelerating the shift to electric transport, buildings and industries. It has received backing from 180 companies with combined annual revenues of $1.69 trillion.
COP31 President Murat Kurum said electrification was essential to strengthen energy security, reduce emissions and support economic growth, particularly amid growing concerns over dependence on imported energy.
The Utilities for Net Zero Alliance (UNEZA) raised its annual investment commitment from $148 billion to $156 billion. The International Energy Agency (IEA) will track progress through a global monitoring mechanism, while the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA) will help developing countries identify investment needs and access financing.
The COP31 presidency is also establishing an Electrify Now Finance Coalition, bringing together governments, development banks and private financial institutions to mobilise funding for emerging and developing economies. The World Bank and African Development Bank are set to serve as its inaugural co-chairs in 2027.
However, campaigners have questioned whether rising electricity demand will be met with renewable energy or additional fossil fuel generation.
Claire Smith of the civil society coalition Beyond Fossil Fuels warned that electrification could increase fossil fuel consumption unless accompanied by renewable energy expansion, stronger grids and storage facilities. The pledge does not explicitly require all additional electricity to come from clean sources, leaving countries to determine their own energy mix.
Türkiye's continued investment in oil and gas has also raised questions about the consistency of its climate ambitions. President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan recently announced two new oil fields with an estimated combined potential of 135 million barrels, while reporting daily production of 84,000 barrels in the Gabar region.
Climate Action Tracker rates Türkiye's overall climate action as “critically insufficient”, citing continued investment in fossil fuels despite progress in wind and solar energy.
The debate has particular significance for developing countries such as Bangladesh, where dependence on imported fossil fuels, limited access to affordable finance and inadequate infrastructure remain major challenges. Expanding renewable energy, upgrading distribution networks and securing technology and investment will be crucial to a sustainable transition.
Further discussions on climate finance are scheduled for November 13. The broader challenge for COP31 will be to turn investment pledges into measurable action and ensure that electrification delivers affordable, reliable and cleaner energy without deepening debt or prolonging fossil fuel dependence.
**This story was produced as part of the COP31 Climate Change Media Partnership, a journalism fellowship organised by Internews' Earth Journalism Network, Informed Earth and the Stanley Center for Peace and Security.

item.title: Dengue: 4 more die, 1,900 hospitalized in 24hrs
item.description:
Four dengue patients died in the last 24 hours till 8am on Wednesday, while 1,900 were hospitalized after being infected with the mosquito-borne disease during the same period.
The latest fatalities have raised the country's dengue death toll to 478 this year, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
Of the newly-hospitalized dengue patients, 780 were in Dhaka Division, 85 in Mymensingh Division, 242 in Chittagong Division, 226 in Khulna Division, 198 in Rajshahi Division, 109 in Rangpur Division, 249 in Barisal Division and 11 in Sylhet Division.
According to the report, a total of 155,668 dengue patients have, so far, been hospitalized across the country this year.
So far, 149,123 dengue patients have recovered and returned home after receiving treatment in the hospitals.
A total of 102,861 people were infected with dengue, and 413 people died from the mosquito-borne disease last year.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 1,295 as six die in 24 hours
item.description:
Six more children have died from measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am on Wednesday, raising the overall death toll from the ongoing outbreak to 1,295.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified all six of the latest casualties as suspected.
With the latest figures, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 1,190, while the number of confirmed deaths remained unchanged at 105, as no new confirmed measles deaths were reported in the last 24 hours.
Among the six new suspected fatalities, the highest concentrations were recorded in the Dhaka and Mymensingh divisions, with two deaths each.
A total of 1,351 suspected measles cases were recorded in the 24 hours till Wednesday morning, taking the overall suspected case tally to 242,907.
During the same period, 113 new confirmed measles cases were reported, bringing the total number of confirmed infections to 24,723.
Since March 15, 2026, a total of 216,806 suspected measles patients have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 207,903 have recovered and been discharged from hospitals, according to the DGHS.

item.title: Iran says tanker struck mine, caught fire in Hormuz
item.description:
Iran’s army said Wednesday that an oil tanker had struck a mine and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, where the country has been targeting ships that transit without its authorization.
Since the outbreak of the Middle East war in late February, Tehran has heavily restricted traffic through the strategic waterway, insisting vessels use routes authorized by the Islamic Republic.
The United States has in response imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports and helped tankers travel the strait, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil.
The American military recently claimed all mines had been cleared from the strait.
“Early this morning, a violating oil tanker caught fire after striking a naval mine in an unsafe, prohibited area in the east of the Strait of Hormuz,” the naval forces of Iran’s army said in a statement carried by state TV.
In recent weeks Tehran has made multiple announcements saying ships had caught fire in the strait, often claiming they struck mines.
US Central Command, which oversees US military operations in the region, has been escorting ships through the waterway and said last month that it had helped Gulf countries export 1.5 billion barrels of oil via Hormuz since the summer.
On Tuesday, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said three oil tankers had caught fire in Hormuz.
India’s shipping minister later said a Liberia-flagged tanker carrying Indian seafarers had been hit by a projectile in the Gulf.
“Four crew members were injured in the attack, including one Indian national, who suffered minor injuries and was safely taken ashore for further medical examination,” Sarbananda Sonowal said in a post on X.
The remaining 18 crew members, including five Indians, were safe, he added.
It was not clear if the tanker was among those the Revolutionary Guards said had been hit.

item.title: Sakhawat: Bangladesh targets universal health coverage by 2030
item.description:
Health and Family Welfare Minister Sardar Md Sakhawat Husain has reaffirmed Bangladesh’s commitment to achieving universal health coverage (UHC) by 2030, saying the government is working to ensure essential healthcare for everyone, regardless of location or social status.
He made the remarks at the first BIMSTEC Health Ministers’ Conference in Colombo, Sri Lanka, attended by health ministers, policymakers and experts from member countries.
Sakhawat highlighted progress in reducing maternal and neonatal mortality, maintaining the country’s polio-free status and expanding immunisation programs.
He said HPV vaccination coverage had risen from 2% to more than 85% since the formation of the new government, with a target of reaching full coverage by the end of November.
The minister said the government, under Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s leadership, had doubled the health sector budget to 1.01% of GDP, with plans to gradually raise it to 5%.
He outlined plans to strengthen preventive and primary healthcare, including establishing primary healthcare centres in more than 4,600 unions and upgrading upazila health complexes from 50 to 151 beds.
Other initiatives include introducing solar power at major government health facilities, improving medical waste management at 15 major hospitals and adopting the One Health approach.
The government is also working to introduce an integrated electronic health record system and unique e-Health IDs to digitise healthcare services.
To strengthen regional health security, Sakhawat proposed setting up a BIMSTEC Regional Genetic Disease Observatory and Early Warning System.

Iran designates Argentina's navy and air force as 'terrorist organisations'
item.description:
Tehran has designated Argentina's navy and air force as "terrorist organisations," Iran's Foreign Ministry said on Wednesday, in a reciprocal move following Buenos Aires' designation of the Islamic Revolutionary Guards as a terrorist entity in April.

Argentina had designated Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) as a terrorist organisation, following a push from US President Donald Trump's administration for allies to do so.

US launches task force to disrupt land transit routes into Iran

Iran's Foreign Ministry said in a statement on Wednesday that Tehran considers the Argentinian air force and navy terrorist organisations "based on the principle of reciprocity".

"It is evident that the responsibility for all consequences arising from this matter will lie with the Argentine government," the ministry added, without elaborating. It made no mention of Argentina's army.

In a statement on Wednesday, Argentina's foreign ministry said it "categorically rejects" Iran's decision.

US offers $20m reward for info on Iran's nuclear program

Argentina said in April that the measure it took against Iran's IRGC was due to its backing for Lebanon-based Hezbollah, which Buenos Aires blames for the deadliest bombing in the South American nation's history, a 1994 attack on the AMIA Jewish community centre in the Argentinian capital that killed 85 and injured hundreds.

The IRGC is an elite military force that protects Shi'ite Muslim clerical rule in Iran and controls large parts of Iran's economy.
